blockers.title: The live NT-3 corpus class has no specification, and NT-3's product law — name, input and pass — appears nowhere in the artifact, so the one statement of the corpus condition is a paraphrase of law the file never quotes
blockers.location: purpose, and the absence of any corpus-class object; retainedEvidence[0].exactByteIntent
blockers.finding: The artifact's own purpose reads: 'State exact-byte intent for every live G25 retained-evidence member AND THE LIVE NT-3 CORPUS CLASS.' It delivers the first half — three members, each with an exactByteIntent and a passProperty — and not the second. There is no corpus-class object anywhere in the file. I enumerated the top-level keys: there is no namedCorpusClasses, no namedCorpusNotAuthored, no liveNtVerbatim, and no class-level exactByteIntent or passProperty. The live harness cell names the corpus the harness executes — 'missing-required-rung corpus (DR-131 NT-3)' — and all the artifact offers for it is namedExecutesLimbs ['NT-3'], a one-sentence disambiguation note, and a suppliedBy string repeated on each member. Naming is not specifying, and this corpus is unspecified. The second limb is what makes it a blocker rather than a structural complaint. I searched the artifact for NT-3's live text and found none of it: the name 'missing-rung-not-success' does not occur; the input 'Required TypeScript semantic universe cannot be constructed.' does not occur; the pass 'Typed Coverage-indeterminate. Not authoritative success. No silent syntax fallback.' does not occur. So the only place the corpus condition is stated at all is EV-1's exactByteIntent, which says 'digest-pinned analyze requests whose required TypeScript semantic rung is absent' — a paraphrase that takes the register's word, 'rung', in place of the product law's own formulation, 'semantic universe cannot be constructed', and the artifact never reconciles the two.
blockers.failureScenario: A fixture author builds the corpus from this specification. The register's formulation points at a project missing one required semantic rung — say type information for a single file, with the rest of the universe constructible. v2's formulation points at a project where the required TypeScript semantic universe cannot be constructed at all — an unresolvable tsconfig, an absent compiler, a project that will not load. Those are different fixtures with different pinned bytes, and one of them may not exercise the property at all: a corpus built to the narrow reading never tests the case v2's NT-3 actually names, while a corpus built to the broad reading may never produce a per-domain Coverage standing for EV-1 to pin. The specification exists to settle exactly that, and it does not, because it never puts the two formulations on the page together.
blockers.whyItMatters: This is the only DR-131 class this gate owns. Every sibling in this lineage reproduces its classes' product law verbatim and then states class-level intent: the G24 sibling carries NT-1 and NT-2 name, input and pass twice each, and gives each class its own exactByteIntent and passProperty; G18 gives each of its three corpus classes both fields; G20 gives its single class both. This candidate is the only one whose corpus has neither, and the one whose corpus is a single class — where the omission is cheapest to fix and most conspicuous.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Add a corpus-class object for NT-3 carrying nameVerbatim, inputVerbatim and passVerbatim quoted from preview-analyze-contract.v2's negativeTests, plus a class-level exactByteIntent and passProperty, in the idiom the G24 sibling already uses on this same contract. Then state which reading of the input the corpus takes — the register's missing rung, v2's unconstructible universe, or both as separate cells — so the paraphrase in EV-1 rests on quoted law rather than replacing it.
blockers.notAClaimThat: I am not asserting the three members are wrong or incomplete against NT-3's pass. I checked that specifically: v2's NT-3 pass has three limbs that map one-to-one onto the three live members. The defect is on the input and class side, not the pass side.

shouldFix.title: EV-1 and EV-3 require the fixture to pin a neighbouring gate's property and then disclaim scoring it, so two members retain bytes that nothing in this specification scores
shouldFix.location: retainedEvidence[0] and retainedEvidence[2], exactByteIntent against passProperty
shouldFix.finding: EV-1's exactByteIntent requires 'pinned Coverage bytes whose standing for that domain is indeterminate — not covered, NOT UNKNOWN-CONVERTED-TO-COVERED, and not omitted'. Its passProperty then reads 'Unknown-to-covered conversion is G23, not this member.' EV-3's exactByteIntent requires 'the terminal preview result showing the invocation is not labeled authoritative success AND IS NOT A SEALED RUN'. Its passProperty then reads 'Silent promotion is G27.' In both cases the retained bytes are specified to demonstrate a property that the member's own pass property hands to another gate. An exact-byte specification exists so that retained evidence and the property that scores it line up; bytes required but unscored are either an unstated obligation on this gate or dead weight in the fixture, and the specification does not say which. The routing itself is correct — unknown-to-covered is DR-G23's live cell and sealed-Run labelling is DR-G27's — so this is a coherence defect inside two members, not a boundary error. The sibling specifications draw the same boundaries without this tension: G24's members separate G29 EE-1 and G30 advertisement in prose and do not require those gates' properties in their retained bytes.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Either drop the neighbouring property from the retained set and leave the boundary as prose, as the siblings do, or keep the bytes and say in the pass property that they are retained as a cross-gate boundary record rather than scored here. One clause either way.

advisories.title: Every self-test convention its siblings carry is absent, and the artifact never names the obligation it would close
advisories.detail: There is no failsIf array, so the artifact exposes none of its own claims to refutation; no whatThisCloses block, so it names no obligation and a later D-000 asked to record this authoring has nothing to record; no global passProperty tying the members to a fixtures-must-exist-first condition; no liveCellMemberSplit, so the three-member decomposition is asserted rather than argued and no invented extra is refused by name; and no proposedLaterWork. There is a genuine upside I want recorded: because it coins no OBL- identifier, it avoids the coined-obligation-on-a-gate-row advisory I have now raised against G07, G18, G20 and G24. But the coordinator should know that this file, unlike those four, offers nothing for a recording act to attach to.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Twelve attacks run, two landed. Custody holds: subject 7ac3ddfd at 0444, 6974 bytes, unmoved and unedited; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26. Five of five cited digests reproduce, including the G23 and G24 sibling subjects it pins. What the candidate carries is accurate. All seven register cells are character-exact against the live row. The three live members split correctly on the semicolon and each has an exactByteIntent, a passProperty and a suppliedBy. The doctor-UNDETERMINED prohibition is answered with a real distinction rather than a denial. And the DR-131 NT-3 versus DR-133 NT-3 collision — which trapped nobody here but is the sharpest hazard in this lineage — is handled better than at any sibling, with the row-local principle stated outright. The blocker is the half of its own purpose it does not deliver. purpose promises exact-byte intent for every live member AND the live NT-3 corpus class. There is no corpus-class object in the file: no namedCorpusClasses, no namedCorpusNotAuthored, no liveNtVerbatim, no class-level intent or pass property. The live harness cell names the corpus this harness executes, and all the artifact gives it is a limb list, a disambiguation sentence and a repeated suppliedBy string. Worse, I searched for NT-3's product law and found none of it: not the name missing-rung-not-success, not the input 'Required TypeScript semantic universe cannot be constructed.', not the pass. So the sole statement of the corpus condition is EV-1's paraphrase — 'analyze requests whose required TypeScript semantic rung is absent' — which substitutes the register's word for the product law's own formulation, and the two are never reconciled. A fixture author cannot tell whether to build a project missing one rung or a project whose semantic universe will not construct at all; those are different fixtures, and one of them may not exercise the property. Settling that is what the specification is for. I checked the other direction and it holds: v2's NT-3 pass has exactly three limbs that map one-to-one onto the three live members, so pass coverage is complete and the defect is on the input and class side only. The SHOULD-FIX is a coherence tension in two members: EV-1 requires the fixture to pin that no unknown-to-covered conversion occurred and then hands that property to G23, and EV-3 requires the result to show it is not a sealed Run and then hands that to G27 — bytes required by the intent that nothing in this specification scores. The routings are right; it is the retain-but-do-not-score that needs one clause either way. Two advisories: every self-test convention the siblings carry is absent — no failsIf, no whatThisCloses, no global passProperty, no punctuation-discipline block — so the artifact exposes none of its own claims and names no obligation for a recorder to attach to, though it does thereby avoid coining a fifth gate-row obligation; and four of the six gate boundaries it disclaims are asserted in a doesNot line without any split drawing them. Both repairs are additive and neither touches the three members, which are sound.
